summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with hands-on embedded software and firmware experience across STM32 Cortex-M4, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Built real-time firmware in bare-metal C and FreeRTOS driving timer-triggered ADC sampling, interrupt-driven UART, multi-servo PWM, and hand-written I2C drivers against custom hardware at deterministic update rates.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback while leading a 25-member team.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Engineered a data pipeline for the BraTS 2020 multi-modal MRI dataset with medical imaging augmentation and batch-loading memory management for 3D volumetric inputs.
Trained and evaluated U-Net segmentation models on Dice Score and IoU; led a cross-functional team of 7 to deliver the full pipeline in a 6-week window.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a PyQt GUI for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a regulated laboratory environment; used GitLab for version control and structured documentation of test results.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi over HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 Cortex-M4 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command parsing and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X time-of-flight sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash and 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a register-level I2C driver; verified end-to-end timing in Proteus before hardware bring-up.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ on the Arduino controller driving five servos, with dual VL53L0X time-of-flight sensors over a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer for range-gated contact detection at 25 mm.

Resolved 11 hardware/software integration failures including servo brown-out, stale-frame capture, and false-positive detection; achieved 100% pick reliability across 10 trials at ~11.5 s end-to-end latency.
